title: Colorado PUC Decision C26-0049: Commission Decision Reopening Proceeding and Remanding to Administrative Law Judge
summary: Commission Decision Reopening Proceeding and Remanding to Administrative Law Judge
text:
Decision No. C26-0049 
BEFORE THE PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION OF THE STATE OF COLORADO 
PROCEEDING NO. 25F-0335EG 
NEVILLE RUSTOMJEE, 
COMPLAINANT, 
V. 
PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY OF COLORADO, 
RESPONDENT. 
COMMISSION DECISION REOPENING PROCEEDING 
AND REMANDING TO ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGE 
Issued Date: 
January 21, 2026 
Adopted Date: January 21, 2026 

I. 
BY THE COMMISSION 
A. 
Statement 
1. 
Through this Decision, the Commission, on its own motion pursuant to 
Rule 1504(b), 4 Code of Colorado Regulations (“CCR”) 723-1, reopens this Proceeding and 
remands the matter to the assigned Administrative Law Judge (“ALJ”). 
2. 
Attached to this Decision as Attachment A is Neville Rustomjee’s (“Complainant”) 
Response to Public Service Company of Colorado’s (“Public Service” or the “Company”) 
Motion to Dismiss Formal Complaint with Prejudice (“Motion to Dismiss”) filed on 
August 27, 2025. Attachment A is entered into the record as evidence in this Proceeding. 
Colorado PUC E-Filings System

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. C26-0049 
PROCEEDING NO. 25F-0335EG 
2 
B. 
Background 
3. 
On August 11, 2025, the Complainant filed a Complaint against Public Service, 
initiating this Proceeding. The Complaint alleged, among other things, that Public Service sent a 
Notice of Disconnection despite all payments being up to date, and requested an order from the 
Commission prohibiting the disconnection of services to his home until resolution of the matter. 
Additionally, the Complaint included various questions addressed to both the Commission and the 
president of Public Service, with a request that they be answered prior to any hearing. 
4. 
On August 13, 2025, Staff of the Public Utilities Commission served a copy of the 
Complaint to Public Service, alongside an order requiring the Company to satisfy or answer the 
Complaint within 20 days, in accordance with § 40-6-108, C.R.S. An evidentiary hearing was 
scheduled for October 27, 2025. 
5. 
On August 27, 2025, the matter was referred by minute entry to an ALJ. 
6. 
On August 27, 2025, Public Service filed its Motion to Dismiss. Public Service 
argued the Complaint must be dismissed because it does not contain sufficient factual allegations 
(accepted as true) to support any plausible claim for relief and that the Complaint does not allege 
any act or omission on Public Service’s part that would violate any provision of law or any order 
or rule of the Commission. 
7. 
The Motion to Dismiss contained a Certificate of Service indicating that the 
document was served upon the Complainant via U.S. Mail. 
8. 
The assigned ALJ issued Decision No. R25-0702EG (“Recommended Decision”) 
on September 30, 2025, granting Public Service’s Motion to Dismiss. The ALJ stated the 
Complainant had failed to file a response and not requested additional time to file a response to 
Public Service’s Motion to Dismiss and therefore dismissed the Complaint with prejudice. 

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. C26-0049 
PROCEEDING NO. 25F-0335EG 
3 
9. 
On October 10, 2025, the Complainant filed exceptions to the Recommended 
Decision, asserting that Public Service’s Motion to Dismiss was not served via U.S. Mail and that 
no copy of the filing was received. The Complainant therefore requested the Recommended 
Decision be set aside and requested an opportunity to respond to the Motion to Dismiss. 
10. 
Public Service responded to the Complainant’s exceptions on October 14, 2025, 
explaining that, in investigating the Complainant’s exceptions, the mail department inadvertently 
did not send the Motion to Dismiss as indicated in the Certificate of Service. Public Service states 
this was unintentional and an administrative oversight, and that upon discovery it has taken action 
to ensure proper service to the Complainant. Given this, Public Service requested the Commission 
reopen the Proceeding to ensure the Complainant has sufficient opportunity to respond to the 
Company’s Motion to Dismiss. 
11. 
Through Decision No. C25-0774, issued October 27, 2025, the Commission 
granted the Complainant’s exceptions, in part, and reopened the Proceeding and remanded the 
matter to the assigned ALJ for further proceedings. 
12. 
Through Decision No. R25-0777-I, issued October 29, 2025, the assigned ALJ 
ordered Public Service to serve the Motion to Dismiss on the Complainant by November 10, 2025. 
The Complainant had until November 24, 2025, to file a response to the Motion to Dismiss. 
13. 
Public Service filed its Notice of Service on November 6, 2025, which indicated 
that the Motion to Dismiss was sent via certified mail and delivered to the Complainant on 
November 1, 2025. 
14. 
Upon not receiving any response from the Complainant, the ALJ, through Decision 
No. R25-0882, issued December 12, 2025, granted Public Service’s Motion to Dismiss and 
dismissed the Complaint with prejudice, and closed the Proceeding. 

Before the Public Utilities Commission of the State of Colorado 
Decision No. C26-0049 
PROCEEDING NO. 25F-0335EG 
4 
15. 
Pursuant to § 40-6-109, C.R.S., Decision No. R25-0882 became a Commission 
Decision on January 1, 2026. 
C. 
Findings and Conclusions 
16. 
Through informal communications, the Commission has been made aware that the 
Complainant physically mailed a Response to the Company's Motion to Dismiss (“Response”) that 
was received by Public Service. The Certificate of Service contained in the Response indicates it 
has been sent via certified mail to the Director of the Commission. 
17. 
The Commission has not received the Complainant’s Response in the mail. 
Using the provided United States Postal Service tracking number,1 it appears the Response was 
delivered to a mailing address in Denver (though a specific address is not provided) on November 
26, 2025. We are unaware whether this Response ever arrived at the Commission. However, even 
if the Commission had received the Complainant’s Response, the filing would have been late as 
the tracking number indicates it was delivered two days after the November 24, 2025 filing 
deadline established in Decision No. R25-0777-I. 
18. 
Subsequently, and again through informal communications, the Commission was 
made aware of a letter from the Complainant which was mailed to and received by Public Service. 
This letter was addressed to the Commission and indicates the Complainant mailed the Response 
to the Commission, has since been in contact with Commission staff regarding the filing of the 
Response, and expresses frustration at the dismissal of the matter. It appears the Complainant 
mistakenly mailed this letter to Public Service rather than the Commission.

19. 
Given the confusion surrounding the receipt—or lack thereof—of the 
Complainant’s filings, and in the interest of ensuring procedural fairness and affording the 
Complainant a full opportunity to be heard, we find good cause to reopen this Proceeding pursuant 
to Rule 1504(b), 4 CCR 723-1. The Complainant’s Response to the Company’s Motion to Dismiss 
is attached as Attachment A to this Decision and is hereby entered into the record in this 
Proceeding. The ALJ may now consider the Complainant’s Response in determining how to move 
forward in this Proceeding and any next procedural steps. 
20. 
While we provide procedural flexibility for the Complainant in this instance, we 
remind the Complainant that Colorado law makes clear that pro se parties are bound by the same 
procedural rules as attorneys.2 We therefore expect all future filings to be timely received by the 
Commission. 
21. 
To avoid similar confusion moving forward, we encourage the Complainant to 
consider using the Commission’s E-Filings system for future filings in this Proceeding, which can 
be accessed using the following link: https://www.dora.state.co.us/pls/efi/EFI.homepage. 
If the Complainant has any questions on how to submit documents through E-Filings, he may 
contact the Commission’s E-Filings Administrator at alison.torvik@state.co.us. To the extent the 
Complainant prefers to use standard mail, we remind the Complainant that filings must be received 
by the Commission by the filing deadline. 

2 E.g., Cornelius v. River Ridge Ranch Landowners Ass’n, 202 P.3d 564, 572 (Colo. 2009); Negron 
v. Golder, 111 P.3d 538, 540 (Colo. App. 2004).

II. 
ORDER 
A. 
The Commission Orders That: 
1. 
Proceeding No. 25F-0335EG is reopened and remanded to the assigned 
Administrative Law Judge for disposition, consistent with the discussion above. 
2. 
Neville Rustomjee’s Response to Public Service Company of Colorado’s Motion 
to Dismiss with Prejudice is attached to this Decision as Attachment A and is now a part of the 
record in this Proceeding. 
3. 
This Decision is effective immediately upon its Issued Date. 
B. 
ADOPTED IN COMMISSIONERS’ WEEKLY MEETING 
JANUARY 21, 2026.
